title: Early Martyrs and Ahmad Shah's Search for the Sikh Raiders

blocks.text: The page first honors a lineage of five early martyrs and nihangs whose memory frames the Khalsa as a community already tested by sacrifice. That commemorative tone matters because it turns the narrative from names of the dead toward the living reputation their courage created.

From there the focus shifts to the enemy court, where Ahmad Shah asks who plundered him and why his forces cannot catch the raiders. The answer presents the Singhs as austere fighters who have no fixed territory, move lightly, and refuse the settled habits that imperial power knows how to punish.

In effect, the page lets even the adversary testify to Sikh resilience. The Khalsa appears not as a conventional kingdom but as a disciplined and elusive force that survives by mobility, hardship, and collective purpose.
